name: pediatric ophthalmology overview
title: A child's eyes: the red reflex sorts a dim or different reflex (refractive error or media opacity), a brighter one (the turned eye in strabismus) and a white one (leukocoria, retinoblastoma first); misaligned eyes are concomitant or incomitant by whether the angle changes with gaze; reduced acuity in one eye without disease is amblyopia; each column gives what is seen, what to think of and what to do, with retinoblastoma (genetics, treatment, outcome) in the leukocoria column

root.title: A child's eyes: acuity in EACH eye, alignment, red reflex
lines: anything that blurs, blocks or misaligns one eye while vision develops → AMBLYOPIA
early detection and early treatment are what restore vision
red reflex: the most important pediatric eye test · no contact, no dilating drops, seconds · ophthalmoscope, retinoscope, flash photos, or parents notice asymmetry
strabismus exam: acuity · obvious turn? · NYSTAGMUS · cardinal gazes · corneal light reflexes · cover test · red reflex

groups.title: RED REFLEX (Brückner): both eyes at once
lines: dim room · 1/3 m or more · child looking far away
~disease in both eyes is easy to miss if they match

groups.title: MISALIGNED: does the angle change with gaze?
lines: corneal light reflexes · cover test (from 6-7 months) · cardinal gazes

groups.title: ACUITY ↓ in one eye
lines: no eye disease to explain it

head: h
Dim or different reflex
pres: • or a visible opacity in it
• the eye with the larger refractive error is dimmer
inv: • abrasion, hyphema, vitreous hemorrhage, retinal pigment change

head: h
Brighter reflex
pres: • finds turns as small as 3 prism dioptres
inv: the BRIGHTER eye is the turned eye
tx: amblyopia risk in the turned eye

head: h
Leukocoria
a WHITE pupillary reflex
pres: • may be the first sign of a life-threatening disease
~physiologic white reflex ~15° off axis: still refer
inv: • 90% no family history: usually ONE eye
• Coats' disease, persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous
• coloboma, familial exudative vitreoretinopathy, retinal detachment, trauma
tx: • diagnosed late: up to 70% die worldwide
more die of a SECOND cancer than of the tumour

head: h
Concomitant strabismus
non-paralytic
pres: • muscles work, eyes not aimed together

head: h
Incomitant strabismus
paralytic or restrictive
pres: a muscle or nerve not working, or tethered

head: h
Amblyopia
↓ acuity, NO organic disease
disrupted visual development · usually one eye, can be both
pres: • to age 2: fusses when the GOOD eye is covered
inv: • refractive: unequal refractive error, the blurrier eye
tx: + glasses (unequal error), or surgery for cataract or strabismus
